chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the sacrificial camel (budn), how is it marked? He said: It is marked while it is tied down, and it is slaughtered while it is standing. It is marked from its right side, and its owner enters into Ihram when it is yoked and marked.

key_terms.تُشْعَرُ: To mark or brand the animal

ai.seo_question: What are the ritual conditions for marking and slaughtering a sacrificial camel in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the precise ritual mechanics for sacrificing a camel (budn), emphasizing that the animal is marked (ushir) while tied down and slaughtered while standing, with the incision made on the right side. It further stipulates that the owner must enter the state of Ihram at the moment the camel is yoked and marked, linking the physical preparation of the animal directly to the pilgrim's spiritual state. This procedure highlights the Shia emphasis on following the Imams' specific instructions regarding the physical handling of sacrificial animals during Hajj.
